## PM claim + dispatch order — R11

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), round **R11**, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-5329-schema-marker-corpus`.

### Two obligations from the comments, both binding

The triage seat states them explicitly and they are the first two things you do:

1. **The canonical `$schema` URL comes from PR #5334 as merged.** ⛔ Read it there. Never re-derive it, never "improve" it, never infer it from the docs site. A marker that differs from what the checker recognises is worse than no marker — it makes 424 files *look* migrated while the recall stays zero.
2. **Re-measure the corpus on current `origin/main` before starting.** The card's table is stamped at `118419214` and says so; more importantly, **#5334 changed which files `objectui check` judges at all**, so the migration surface may be materially smaller than the card's ~424. The unlock comment flags this in terms: *"the ~424-file corpus figure in this card's body is the first thing to re-measure."*

Report your measured number against the card's, and if they differ, say why rather than adopting either.

### Scope

The producer-side half of #5127's Option B: give the in-repo schema corpus the canonical marker so `objectui check` recognises the files it is supposed to judge. Acceptance is the **D-arm skipped-file count** — that is the number this card moves, so measure it before and after and lead with it.

⛔ Out of scope: the checker itself (#5334 landed it), the consumer-side half, and any file that is not an ObjectUI schema. ⚠️ Do not add the marker to a file merely to make a count go up — a marker on a non-schema file is a false positive the checker will then judge, and that is a defect this card would be introducing.

### Verification this card owes

- **Before/after D-arm skipped-file count**, with the command that produced each.
- A mechanical check on your own diff, at this scale: every changed file's diff is *only* the marker addition, with a histogram to prove it. A 400-file sweep is exactly where a regex quietly does something else — PR #5369 set the standard here (412 changed line pairs, 0 non-conforming, histogram reported), and this card is the same shape.
- **Non-vacuity**: prove the marker is actually recognised. Show one file the checker skipped before and judges after, and — the control — show that a file with a *wrong* marker is still skipped, so "judged" is attributable to the canonical value rather than to the presence of any `$schema` key.
- JSON validity across every touched file (a marker inserted into malformed position is a parse error, not a migration).
- The repo's own gates per your diff; run vitest from the repo root, not package-scoped.

⛔ Never `git stash` — the stack is shared across worktrees and other agents are using it right now.

Refs: #5127 · PR #5334 · #5329's own stamped table.

## Dev report — R11 · `needs_decision` · premise falsified

**No PR. No files changed.** The card's deliverable cannot be executed as specified, and the reason is in PR #5334 as merged — exactly where obligation ① sent me to look.

### Obligation ① — the canonical `$schema` URL from PR #5334 as merged

I read it there. **There is no URL.** PR #5334's merged body, verbatim:

> ⛔ **No permanent public identifier is proposed any more.** The URL this PR previously proposed for confirmation is **not adopted** and appears nowhere in the code, the skip hint, the tests, the changeset or the docs.

The maintainer's **2026-08-20 ruling (verbatim 「C」) superseded the `$schema` half** of the 2026-08-19 「全部接受」 ruling that created this card. `pointsAtObjectUi()` and `OBJECTUI_SCHEMA_URL` were deleted before merge. The merged `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts` carries a 25-line comment block headed:

> `⛔ There is deliberately NO $schema arm, and no ObjectUI $schema URL exists to declare.`

The only marker the shipped checker honours is a **root structural key** from a closed 14-item set (`body`, `children`, `className`, `style`, `placeholder`, `visible`, `visibleWhen`, `visibleOn`, `hidden`, `hiddenOn`, `disabled`, `disabledOn`, `testId`, `ariaLabel`). The PR-#5334 head branch is deleted and the constant is unreachable from `main`, so there is no historical spelling to recover either.

### Obligation ② — re-measured corpus on current `origin/main` (`a1c41c516`)

| | card (@ `118419214`) | #5334 (@ `9f118b934`) | **now (`a1c41c516`)** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| files analysed | — | 612 | **617** |
| **D-arm skipped** | — | 304 | **309** |
| eligible (root `type`) | — | 470 | **475** |
| real schema files | ~424 | 424 | **429** |
| — real judged | — | 166 | **166** |
| — real skipped | — | 258 | **263** |
| foreign skipped | — | 46 | **46** |

**The surface did not shrink — it grew.** The unlock comment's hypothesis ("may be materially smaller") is falsified: the catalog gained 5 files (423 → 428 schemas), so real-skipped went 258 → 263. Foreign skipped is unchanged at 46 (45 `package.json` `"type":"module"` + the one draft-07 document `packages/vscode-extension/schemas/objectui-schema.json`). 263 + 46 = 309. ✓

Command for every count above: `node packages/cli/dist/cli.js check` from the repo root, after `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build && pnpm --filter @object-ui/cli build`. My independent harness reproduces the CLI's own 617/309 exactly, so the breakdown is faithful.

**0 of the 429 real corpus files declare `$schema` today.**

### The decisive experiment — a `$schema` sweep is a measured no-op

Paired ablation on one currently-skipped real file, `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/plugin-view/object-view-record-surface.json`. Same file, same build, same command; only the injected key differs. Each leg carried a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restore, and each mutation was confirmed on disk by `grep -c` on the injected text plus `git diff --numstat` before reading any result.

| leg | injected at root | mutation on disk | D-arm skipped |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | — | — | **309** |
| A | `"$schema": "https://objectui.org/schema/v1/schema.json"` | confirmed, 1 occurrence | **309** — *no movement* |
| B (positive control) | `"className": ""` | confirmed, 1 occurrence | **308** — *moved by exactly 1* |

Restore legs verified byte-identical: `git status --porcelain` empty and the marker greps to **0** after each. Leg B proves the harness can detect a single file changing state, so leg A's flat 309 is a real measurement, not a probe that missed.

**Stamping the canonical marker into 429 files would move the acceptance number by zero** — precisely the failure mode the dispatch order warned about ("makes 424 files LOOK migrated while recall stays zero"), except here it holds for *any* `$schema` value, because there is no arm to match one.

### Why there is no in-scope way to move the count

The 263 skipped real files are genuinely leaf/config-shaped, confirming the card's own structural analysis. Root-key-count histogram: 189 of 263 have ≤4 root keys (1 key: 3 · 2: 43 · 3: 72 · 4: 71 · 5: 51 · 6+: 23). Dominant roots are `form` (81, keyed `fields`/`showSubmit`/`showCancel`) and `button` (25, keyed `label`/`variant`/`onClick`) — real ObjectUI vocabulary, none of it in the structural set.

The only two ways to move the number are both out of scope:

1. **A `$schema` arm** — the maintainer ruled against it on 2026-08-20 and #5334 records the reasoning in the code.
2. **Widening the structural key set** to admit `fields`, `label`, `variant`, `onClick` — that is *the checker itself*, explicitly out of scope, and #5334 measured `label` as one of the keys held out by name because admitting it re-creates foreign retention.

Injecting `"className": ""` into 263 leaf schemas to trip the heuristic is not a migration — it is fabricating presentational content into the corpus to move a count, which is the thing the dispatch order forbids.

### The contradiction that needs the maintainer

`check.ts` promises, in the comment beside the gate, that the debt is repayable:

> ⚠️ The structural arm is a TRANSITIONAL fallback, not the contract… a real schema wrongly skipped is a coverage debt **that the corpus migration repays** and that the skipped-file count below keeps visible in the meantime.

But the same PR deleted the only mechanism by which a corpus migration *could* repay it. That contradiction is live in merged code, and resolving it is a public-contract decision, not a sweep.

### The card's claimed side benefit is also false

The card says migration "should also buy editor autocomplete and validation" via `packages/vscode-extension/schemas/objectui-schema.json`. It would not:

- The extension binds by **filename glob**, not `$schema` — `contributes.jsonValidation.fileMatch` is `*.objectui.json` / `*.oui.json`.
- **0 of 429** corpus files match either glob.
- The bundled schema declares **no `$id`**, so no `$schema` URL could resolve to it regardless.

### Files deliberately left unmarked

**All 429.** No file received a marker. The 46 foreign files are correctly skipped and must stay that way — marking any of them would be the false positive the dispatch order names as a defect.

## PM ruling: **option A** — closing as superseded. The card asks for a marker that does not exist.

This is the correct outcome and the dev reached it by doing exactly what the dispatch order's first obligation said: *"the canonical `$schema` URL comes from PR #5334 as merged — read it there, never re-derive."* Reading it there is how the card fell over.

### What the merged code actually says

There is **no ObjectUI `$schema` URL**. The maintainer's 2026-08-20 ruling (verbatim **C**) superseded the `$schema` half of the 2026-08-19 ruling, and #5334 **deleted `OBJECTUI_SCHEMA_URL` and `pointsAtObjectUi()` before merge**. `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts` on `main` states there is deliberately no `$schema` arm and no URL to declare.

So the card's central instruction — stamp the canonical marker into the corpus — names an identifier that was removed from the codebase four days ago. Had the dev "re-derived" or "improved" a URL, this PR would have stamped 429 files with a string nothing recognises: a corpus that **looks** migrated while recall stays exactly zero. That is the precise failure the obligation was written to prevent, and it earned its keep here.

### Proved empirically, not by reading — which is what makes this conclusive

A code reading alone could be wrong about behaviour. The dev ran a **paired ablation** on a real currently-skipped file:

| leg | injected | D-arm skipped |
|---|---|---:|
| A | `"$schema": "https://objectui.org/schema/v1/schema.json"` | **309** — unmoved |
| B (positive control) | `"className": ""` (a structural key) | **308** — moved by exactly 1 |

Leg B is what makes leg A a **measurement rather than a probe that missed**: the harness demonstrably detects a single file changing state, so the flat reading in leg A is a real absence. A corpus-wide sweep is a measured no-op on this card's own acceptance criterion.

Both legs carried `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restores, each mutation was confirmed on disk with `grep -c` plus `git diff --numstat` **before any result was read**, and both restores verified byte-identical. And an independent harness reproducing the gate's predicate matched the CLI exactly (617 globbed / 475 eligible / 166 judged / 309 skipped = 263 real + 46 foreign), so the instrument was validated against the thing it was measuring.

### Obligation 2 also inverted the card's assumption

Re-measured on `origin/main`: the surface **grew** rather than shrank — **429** real files / **263** real-skipped / **309** D-arm, against the card's ~424 / 258 / 304. The unlock comment predicted the migration surface "may be materially smaller"; it is larger. Either way the card's stamped table is stale, which is why re-measuring was mandatory.

### The card's claimed side benefit does not exist either

Worth recording, because it removes the last argument for doing this anyway: **0 of 429** in-repo files declare an ObjectUI `$schema` today, and the VS Code extension binds by **filename glob** (`contributes.jsonValidation.fileMatch` on `*.objectui.json` / `*.oui.json`), not by `$schema` — with **0 of 429** corpus files matching either glob and no `$id` in the bundled schema. So editor validation would not light up from this sweep.

### Why A rather than B, C or D

- **B** (mint the URL after all) reopens a decision the maintainer closed four days ago with the reasons recorded in code, and those reasons still hold. Not a lane-PM call, and nothing here is new evidence.
- **C** (widen `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS` to admit leaf vocabulary) is a change to **the checker, not the corpus** — a different card. #5334 measured `label` as held out **by name** precisely because admitting `BaseSchema`-adjacent naming keys drives foreign retention from 0 files toward all 46. It needs per-key foreign-retention measurement before anyone commits.
- **D** (inject structural keys to move the count) is rejected, and the dev was right to list it only to record that it was considered and refused. It fabricates presentational content into the corpus to satisfy a heuristic and changes rendered output — the literal *"do not add the marker merely to make a count go up"* prohibition from this card's dispatch order.

Closing this card as **superseded**, not as done: nothing was delivered because nothing could be.

### Two follow-ups filed

- The **263-file recall debt is real and stays open** — closing this card must not make it disappear. Filed as a tracking card blocked on `@object-ui/types` shipping a generated JSON Schema, which is what #5334 itself names as the soundest trigger for adding a `$schema` arm later. That decision is already in the queue as **#5392**. Because matching would be host-based, the arm can be added then **without invalidating a single file** — so waiting costs nothing and forecloses nothing.
- **`check.ts` carries a now-false promise** that *"the corpus migration repays"* the recall debt, when merged code removed the mechanism that migration would use. Filed as its own small, immediately-actionable card; that comment is wrong today regardless of which route the debt eventually takes.

⛔ No files changed, no PR opened, final diff 0 lines. No repo gates were owed and none are claimed.

## Closing as superseded — completing a state transition the record already describes

Closed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R30. ⚠️ **This is a half-state repair, not a new judgement**, so the sourcing comes first.

### Where the decision to supersede this card was already made

Two cards filed by the previous seat (session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`) on 2026-08-24 both describe this card in the past tense as already closed:

- **#6074**, opening line: *"Filed … as the immediately-actionable follow-up promised when **#5329** was closed as superseded."* — since merged as PR #6079.
- **#6075**, opening line: *"Filed … as the tracking follow-up promised when **#5329** was closed as superseded."* — now `pm:queue` and dispatched this round.

Both successors exist, one has landed, and this card carries `pm:dispatched` with an assignee while every other record treats it as finished. That is the half-state: an open, claimed card that nothing is working and that two other cards describe as closed.

### The premise, verified on `main` rather than inherited

`origin/main` @ `090927f4f`, `packages/cli`:

- probe — `OBJECTUI_SCHEMA_URL` / `pointsAtObjectUi`: the only hit in the whole package is `check.ts:112`, a **comment recording that both were deleted before #5334 merged**. No implementation remains.
- control — `OBJECTUI_STRUCTURAL_KEYS`: present at `:35`, `:128`, `:255`.

The control is what makes the probe a reading rather than a mis-escaped grep.
